lessons.title: Reversing the Product Rule
lessons.focus: deriving and applying integration by parts from the product rule
lessons.solution1: Take u=x and dv=e^x dx; the result is xe^x−e^x+C=e^x(x−1)+C.

lessons.title: Choosing u and dv Strategically
lessons.focus: selecting factors so differentiation simplifies and integration remains possible
formulas: LIATE is a heuristic, not a theorem
lessons.solution1: Use u=ln x and dv=dx; result xln x−x+C.
lessons.solution2: Use u=ln x, dv=x²dx; result x³ln x/3−x³/9+C.

lessons.title: Applications, Method Comparison & Proof of Verification
lessons.focus: defending method choice and validating integration-by-parts results
lessons.example1: Evaluate ∫₁^e ln x dx and interpret the signed area.
lessons.example2: Explain why choosing u=e^x and dv=x dx is less efficient for ∫x e^x dx.
lessons.solution2: Differentiating e^x does not simplify it, while integrating x increases degree; the alternative u=x immediately lowers complexity.
